RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL   ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday,  the March 14, 2006/Phalguna 23, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Finance; Heavy Industries and
Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas; Tourism and Culture;
Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
Parking facility for private planes
*321. SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
 Will the Minister of  CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether a large number of Corporate
Houses are rushing in to buy business jets
and turbo prop planes for their top brass
and also queuing up to park at the hangars
at the Airports;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) what action Government propose
to take to accommodate such private planes
at the Airports?
Fake notes through ATM
†*322. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
SHRIMATI JAYA
BACHCHAN:
 Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the incidents
of finding fake notes through ATM
machines of various banks have been
brought to the notice of Government;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the details of banks brought to the
notice of Government where such incidents
had taken place; and
(d) the action taken by Government
against the guilty persons?
Rate of interest on loans by NABARD
*323. SHRI N.K.
PREMACHANDRAN:
SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR:
 Will the Minister of  FINANCE be
pleased to state:
(a) the interest rate allowed by the
NABARD for the agricultural loans;
(b) whether Government are aware that
the interest rate exceeds when the agriculture
loans of NABARD are routed through the
Co-operative and other commercial banks
for the agriculture; and
(c) whether Government consider to
extend the agricultural loans to farmers at
the interest rate prescribed by the
NABARD and the reaction of Government
thereto?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

101
Excavations undertaken by ASI
*324. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR:
Will the Minister of  TOURISM AND
CULTURE  be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Archaeological Survey
of India (ASI) has undertaken excavations
during the last two years;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise;
and
(c) the details of new discoveries of
historic significance made during the
excavations by the different circles?
Progress of water management
programmes
*325. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA:  Will
the Minister of  WATER RESOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that restructured
Command Area Development and Water
Management Programmes have not achieved
the desired results and it is progressing at
snail's speed;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) what was the total area in which the
work has been completed under the said
programme so far; and
(d) the steps being taken by
Government to accelerate the speed of work
under the said programme?
Increase in revenue from petroleum
products
†*326. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
 Will the Minister of  FINANCE  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that despite low
rate of tax on petroleum in the year
2005-06, the tax revenue is estimated to be
rupees 5,115 crores;
(b) if not, what are Government's
estimate in this regard, and whether this
amount is more than the revenue amount
of 4699 crore rupees in the year 2004-2005;
and
(c) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons for which the revenue amount
during this year is more as compared to
that of last year?
New guidelines for penalties for adultera-
tion in fuel by dealer/petrol pumps
*327. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
Will the Minister of  PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that penalties for
adulteration in fuel by dealer/petrol pump
operators have been reduced/weakened
under new guidelines;
(b) what were the penalties for adulteration
earlier and what are they now; and
(c) what are the reasons for reducing
them?
Production of bio-diesel
*328. DR. NARAYAN SINGH
MANAKLAO:  Will the Minister of
PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government consider higher
production of bio-diesel as substitute to
petroleum, keeping in view the spiraling
global petroleum prices;
(b) if so, the steps taken in this regard;
(c) the comparative cost of importing
petroleum and producing bio-diesel;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

102
(d) whether Government propose to
encourage R&D in inventing petroleum
substitute;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) if not, the reasons therefor and the
strategy to meet the future requirement?
Future projections of domestic and
Foreign Direct Investment
*329. SHRIMATI MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
 Will the Minister of  FINANCE  be
pleased to state:
(a) when he proposes to actually
translate his declared assertion that  India
has a competitive advantage in areas of
manufacturing, services, BPO sectors etc.
by ensuring greater investment both
domestic and FDI; and
(b) what is the projected investments
in these sectors during 2006-07 especially
when considerable groundwork has been
done by Government during the current
fiscal?
Financial aid to Andhra Pradesh by
ADB
*330. SHRI RA VULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY:  Will the Minister of
FINANCE  be pleased to state:
(a) the number of schemes being
implemented by Government through the
financial assistance from ADB in Andhra
Pradesh;
(b) the details of such financial
assistance taken for Andhra Pradesh;
(c) the amount allocated for each project;
(d) the present status of each project;
(e) whether the ADB has expressed
satisfaction in regard to utilization of the
amount;
(f) if so, the details thereof; and
(g) the interest paid to ADB for each
project so far?
Companies in Andhra Pradesh
vanishing with investors money
†*331.  SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH:
Will the Minister of  COMPANY
AFFAIRS  be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the companies in
Andhra Pradesh that vanished with the
money of common investors during the last
three years;
(b) the number of companies whose
promoters/directors were prosecuted
against and the number of those punished
during the said period;
(c) the number of legal professionals
engaged in Andhra Pradesh to fight the cases
against such companies;
(d) the procedure of drawing panel of
such legal professionals;
(e) whether Government propose to
appoint more legal professionals in  Andhra
Pradesh to dispose off such cases
expeditiously; and
(f) if so, the details in this regard?
Condition of Almatti Dam
*332.  SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:  Will
the Minister of  WATER RESOURCES
be pleased to state:
(a) whether following the recent heavy rains
and flood devastation in Mumbai and areas
around, Government have caused thorough
check of the condition of Almatti Dam;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

103
(b) if so, how far it is in good condition
and what upgradation and augmentation is
considered necessary to ensure that the dam
is able to withstand future onslaught and
natural calamity;
(c) the estimated cost of such
augmentation of the dam; and
(d) the Central aid sought and given for
the same?
Tax free interest on term deposits
†*333.  SHRI UDAY PRATAP SINGH:
Will the Minister of  FINANCE  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are
contemplating to make interest on term
deposits tax free; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and by when
it would be effective?
Rate of inflation
†*334. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of  FINANCE  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the inflation
rate in the country has been estimated to
be at 5 or 5.5 per cent;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
increase in the prices of items like flour,
rice, milk, pulses, fruits, vegetables used in
daily food of common man is more than
above quoted rate; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Loans under PMRY to Bihar
†*335.  SHRI SHA TRUGHAN
SINHA:  Will the Minister of  FINANCE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
only 13 per cent of the target to provide
loan under the Pardhan Mantri Rozgar
Yojna has been achieved in Bihar, whereas
the target has been enhanced by 35 per
cent during the financial year 2005-06;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the steps being taken by
Government to improve the situation?
Cracks in Sun Temple at Konark
*336. SHRIMATI JAYA
BACHCHAN:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the Minister of  TOURISM AND
CULTURE  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the 12th
Century Sun Temple at Konark, Orissa has
developed cracks;
(b) if so, the reasons for such happening
and details in this regard; and
(c) the action taken to restore/repair the
Temple?
Excise package for Kutch area
*337.  SHRI RAJU PARMAR:  Will
the Minister of  FINANCE  be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Gujarat has represented to the Central
Government to extend the liberal benefits
of excise package to Kutch area as has been
extended to Sikkim, Uttaranchal, Jharkhand
and Himachal Pradesh; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

104
(b) if so, what is the response of the
Central Government thereto?
Funds for tourism related
infrastructure
*338.  SHRI C. PERUMAL:  Will the
Minister of  TOURISM AND CULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry has requested
each Ministry to set aside a certain portion
of their funds for tourism related
infrastructure; and
(b) if so, the reaction of each Ministry
thereon?
Shortage of 25 and 50 paise coins in
Karnataka
*339.  SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY:  Will the Minister of
FINANCE  be pleased to state:
(a) whether 25 and 50 paise coins are
withdrawn from circulation in Karnataka;
(b) if not, what are the reasons for the
shortage of these lower denomination coins
in Karnataka;
(c) whether Government are aware that
in Karnataka, public have been given other
goods in return for the balance amount; and
(d) the steps proposed to be taken to
ensure proper supply of these coins in
Karnataka if they are not withdrawn?
GAIL's project in Kerala
*340.  SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of  PETROLEUM AND
NATURAL GAS  be pleased to state:
(a) whether GAIL has signed a
memorandum of cooperation during the
year 2004 for setting up a petrochemical
project at Kochi, Kerala;
(b) if so, the present status of the above
project;
(c) the details of fiscal concessions
sought from the State Government of
Kerala and those actually granted for the
above project;
(d) the details of the expected
completion of the project; and
(e) the details of feedstock for the
project and the source of fuel for the
project?
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 8th March, 2006  Secretary-General.

RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, the March 14, 2006/Phalguna 23, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Finance; Heavy Industries and
Public Enterprises; Petroleum and Natural Gas; Tourism and Culture;
Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 155
Losses due to strike by AAI employees
†2246. SHRI LAXMINARAYAN
SHARMA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) the losses suffered by Government
due to strike in the first week of February,
2006 in protest against handing over Delhi
and Mumbai airports to the private sector;
and
(b) whether sufficient efforts were not
made earlier to avoid the said strike?
Shortage of parking bays at Mumbai
Airport
2247. SHRI RAJ KUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Mumbai
Airport does not have adequate number of
parking bays for aircrafts for night parking;
(b) if so, whether airlines have been
asked by AAI to park aircrafts overnight at
neighbouring airports like Pune,
Ahmedabad etc.; and
(c) what is the response of the airlines
to this request?
Direct air service between Amritsar
and London
2248. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal to
start direct flights from Amritsar to London
in near future;
(b) the status of the proposal; and
(c) by when, inaugural flight is likely to
start?
Construction of bays at airports
2249. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Airports
Authority of India is in the process of
construction of 143 bays at 45 airports;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

506
(c) the details of non-metro airports that
are proposed to be upgraded to world-class
standards indicating those falling in the State
of Orissa?
Expenditure incurred on training of
pilots
2250. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the amount incurred by Government
on the training of pilots of Government
owned airlines during each of the last three
years;
(b) whether Government are aware that
these pilots are lured by private airlines
with lucrative offers;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the steps being taken by
Government for the protection of interests
of the pilots and also Government owned
airlines?
Guidelines on helicopter operations
2251. SHRI R.P. GOENKA : Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that revised
comprehensive guidelines have been issued
recently to tighten the norms for helicopter
operations in the country; and
(b) if so, the details thereof, especially
those relating to assessment of weather
forecasting in the hilly areas where weather
can change very fast?
Sanction of a new modern airport for
Chennai
2252. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether there is a move for sanction
of a new Modern International airport for
Chennai as has been done for Bangalore in
the wake of heavy spurt and steep increase
of traffic in Chennai due to the growth of
information technology, the proposal of
diverting all flights bound for South-East
Asian countries through Chennai Airport
and the need of patients from Asian
countries for fairly cheap and qualitative
treatment at Chennai; and
(b) whether the Chief Minister of Tamil
Nadu has already raked up a proposal for a
new airport at the cost of around Rs. 1000
crores in an extent of 2000 acres?
New International airports
2253. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the names of airports which were
given the status of international airports
during the last three years;
(b) whether Government propose to
declare some more airports as international
airports; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Slow progress of airport
modernisation
2254. SHRIMATI JAYA
BACHCHAN: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government

507
are moving at a snail's pace so far as
modernisation of country's airports is
concerned; and
(b) if so, the reasons therefor?
Flying requirement for issue of
licence
2255. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the pilots including in
private airlines are not fully acquiring the
flying experience as stipulated in Civil
Aviation rules; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor?
Revamping of boards of IA and AI
2256. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any plan
to revamp the boards of IA and AI;
(b) whether it is a fact that as a part of
revamping Government are thinking of
appointing functional directors;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether any consultations with the
Public Enterprises Selection Board have
been held in this regard; and
(e) if so, what is the outcome of the
consultation process?
New airports
2257. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether any fresh initiatives have
been taken by Government during the last
one year to open up more airports in
various cities of the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Criteria for upgradation of airports
2258. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to refer to answer
to Unstarred Question 189 given in the
Rajya Sabha on the 21st February 2006
and state:
(a) the details of the existing airports
recently upgraded into international
airports with criteria adopted for such
upgradation;
(b) whether such upgradation is
contemplated in respect of other airports,
including Mangalore Airport and set-up
new airports at other locations; and
(c) if so, the details with the reasons
and the time-frame for completion of each
project?
Development of Belgaum airport
2259. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Karnataka has requested the Central
Government to take up the improvement
of terminal building and security measures
of the Belgaum airport in Karnataka;
(b) if so, the estimated cost of the
proposed works; and
(c) what is the present position?

508
Private airline operators
2260. SHRI TARINI KANTA ROY:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) following acquisition of Sahara
Airlines by Jet Airways, how many
companies are presently operating in
domestic air market; and
(b) the percentage of their market share,
company-wise?
Funds for modernisation of airports
2261. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are contemplating modernisation of airports
apart from Delhi and Mumbai;
(b) if so, the details thereof indicating
time-frame for the same; and
(c) the estimated funds needed to be
invested towards the same with its probable
sources?
Development of aviation sector in
Uttaranchal
2262. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will the
Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to develop the aviation sector in Uttaranchal
from the tourism point of view in the hilly
state;
(b) if so, in what manner;
(c) whether some proposals of the State
Government in this regard are pending with
the Centre;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) by when, these schemes will be
materialized?
Opposition to sell-off of public utility
services
2263. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that airport unions
have opposed sell-off of public utility
services in the field of aviation;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) Government's reaction thereto?
Development of Mangalore airport
2264. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have identified
Mangalore (Bajpe) airport for development
under Phase-I of the non-metro airports
development programme;
(b) whether the Expression of Interest
(EoI) for architectural design has been
received from bidders and evaluated for the
project; and
(c) by when the work on development
is likely to be started by AAI?
Facilities at overseas IA offices
2265. SHRI VARINDER SINGH
BAJWA: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) what steps Government have taken
to improve the passenger amenities at IA
offices/counters at UK, USA and other
major countries;

509
(b) whether Government have received
complaints/suggestions in this regard from
some Members of Parliament in 2005; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Theft cases at Airports
†2266. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is threat
to security as a result of increasing incidents
of theft at various airports of the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action being taken by
Government to tackle the said problem?
Training to Pilots
†2267. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether pilots are not being trained
as compared to the increasing number of
aeroplanes and passengers in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps being taken by
Government to fill up this gap?
Demand for pilots
2268. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the demands for pilots in
the next four years may reach more than
three thousands;
(b) if so, whether we have capacity to
produce such numbers of expected pilots
in the next four years;
(c) whether Government are planning
to start new Aeronautics training schools;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Inquiry into IPO Scam
2269. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of COMPANY
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether he has recently indicated
that his Ministry propose to look into the
recent IPO scam;
(b) if so, whether this enquiry would be
independent of the inquiries being
conducted by the RBI and SEBI; and
(c) if so, the details of its terms of
reference?
Dual responsibility of investors
2270. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR: Will the Minister of
COMPANY AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that some of the
institutional investors in the country have
fiduciary responsibility while many
investors have only corporate
responsibility in terms of protecting the
return on their investments;
(b) if so, whether Government propose
to address this dichotomy with details
thereof; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

510
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Grants-in-aid for tricentenary
anniversary of Gur-Ta-Gaddi
2271. SHRI PRAMOD MAHAJAN:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Maharashtra has sought sanction of
maximum grant-in-aid for tricentenary
anniversary of Gur-Ta-Gaddi at Nanded
city; and
(b) if so Central Government's reaction
thereto?
Smuggling of currency to Hong Kong
2272. SHRIMATI JAYA
BACHCHAN: Will the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Indian
currency is being freely traded in Hong Kong
these days;
(b) whether it is also a fact that Indians
are not allowed to take with them Indian
currency abroad; and
(c) whether Government have the
circumstances in which the Indian currency
was smuggled abroad and if so, with what
results?
Banking operations by foreign
companies
2273. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of FINANCE
be pleased to state:
(a) where overseas financial companies
are evincing interest in setting up banking
operations in the country;
(b) if so, the details of such proposals
received and approved so far;
(c) the details of FDI limits and other
terms and conditions, including priority
lending norms, that the promoters are
required to adhere to before and after being
permitted to establish banking operations
in the country;
(d) whether it is a fact that sector
specific priority lending norm and double
taxation are some of the issues inhibiting
banking operation by foreign entities in the
country; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and
Governments reaction thereto?
Indirect tax rate
2274. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the country
has the highest indirect tax rate;
(b) if so, the details thereof, sector-wise;
and
(c) whether Government propose to
launch schemes for poor people by which
they have to pay less indirect taxes?
Non-spending of budget allocation by
Ministries
2275. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that as per the
latest figures available with the Comptroller
General of Accounts (CGA), many
Ministries have not spent the budget
allocated to them in the Plan expenditure
for the year 2005-06; and
(b) if so, the action Government
propose to take to encourage the Ministries

511
to spend the entire amount of allocated
funds?
Withdrawal of guarantee on LIC
policies
2276. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA:
SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD :
Will the Minister of FINANCE be
pleased to state :
(a) whether the private life insurance
sector has complained to IRDA that
Government guarantee on more than 16
crore policies sold by LIC has created a
bias for LIC policies among the public;
(b) whether Government propose to
withdraw  its guarantee on LIC policies in
view of LIC having met the IRDA’s
solvency margin last year;
(c) whether the withdrawal of
Government guarantee on LIC policies
require an amendment to the LIC Act; and
(d) whether such withdrawal of
Government guarantee on LIC policies will
change the character of security of the
existing policies?
Requirement of cash withdrawal
reporting by banks
2277. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD : Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state :
(a) whether cash withdrawals from
current accounts in banks mostly become a
part of the black economy and if so, whether
to establish the trail such transactions lead
to, Government have imposed cash
withdrawal tax;
(b) whether most of the Public Sector
Banks, Regional Rural banks and banks in
private sector/co-operative sector are
complying with the requirements of
reporting such transactions to the Income
Tax Department; and
(c) whether most of the Regional Rural
Banks are lagging behind in complying with
the requirement of cash withdrawal
reporting?
Bringing more service providers
under tax net
2278. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state :
(a) whether it is a fact that the Central
Board of Excise and Customs is considering
to bring more service providers under the
tax net;
